League+]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best [[power forward]]s in the 2020 class. A former [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] commit, Todd chose to forgo his [[college basketball|college]] eligibility to become the last player to sign with [[NBA G League Ignite]] before it ceased operations. He finished his high school career at the [[Word of God Christian Academy]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Baltimore|Baltimore, Maryland]], Todd was raised by his mother, Marlene Venable, and did not know his father well. His mother sold [[cocaine]] and [[heroin]] at age twelve and served over three years in prison when she was sixteen. She was released from prison about four years before Todd's birth. When Todd started playing basketball, at age seven, he stood five feet tall.{{cite web |last1=Kolenich |first1=Eric |title=John Marshall's Isaiah Todd — the top-ranked high school basketball player in the country — was shaped by his mother and her past life of crime |url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/high-school/john-marshall-s-isaiah-todd-the-top-ranked-high-school/article_f171cb0a-2364-11e8-b843-1f2f08644215.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=March 9, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Isaiah Todd |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/t/todd-isaiah.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921042239/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/t/todd-isaiah.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 21, 2019 |website=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=December 4, 2019}} At that age, he met his first coach, Derrick Wilson, and began playing on recreational teams and on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit. Before eighth grade, Todd moved to [[Richmond, Virginia]] so that he could play year-round for his AAU program, Team Loaded. ==High school career== In his first two years of high school, Todd played basketball for [[John Marshall High School (Richmond, Virginia)|John Marshall High School]] in Richmond. As a freshman, he averaged 12.8 points and 6.5 rebounds per game, leading his team to district and regional titles. Todd was considered one of the area's best prospects since [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Basketball Hall of Fame]] inductee [[Moses Malone]].{{cite web |last1=Jeter |first1=Fred |title=Tall men help John Marshall open season with wins |url=http://richmondfreepress.com/news/2016/dec/16/tall-men-help-john-marshall-open-season-wins/ |website=[[Richmond Free Press]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=December 16, 2016}}{{cite web |last1=Kolenich |first1=Eric |title=John Marshall's Isaiah Todd and Trinity's Armando Bacot are rarities in high school basketball |url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/john-marshall-s-isaiah-todd-and-trinity-s-armando-bacot/article_9d1d600c-d4c5-11e7-8103-1fc9c9685e2a.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=November 29, 2017}} As a sophomore, Todd averaged 18.6 points, 6.5 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game, shooting 39 percent from three-point range, to help John Marshall win the Class 3 state championship.{{cite web |last1=Kolenich |first1=Eric |title=John Marshall basketball player Isaiah Todd will transfer to North Carolina |url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/high-school/john-marshall-basketball-player-isaiah-todd-will-transfer-to-north/article_ff80c70a-456f-11e8-97e0-0b4fda36df82.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=April 21, 2018}} He was recognized as the Class 3 State Player of the Year and earned first-team All-Metro honors.{{cite web |last1=Kolenich |first1=Eric |title=The 2018 All-Metro boys basketball team |url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/high-school/basketball/the-all-metro-boys-basketball-team/article_3115588c-355b-11e8-a30e-1fd55d64357f.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=March 31, 2018}} For his junior season, Todd transferred to [[Trinity Academy (Raleigh, North Carolina)|Trinity Academy]], a private [[Christian school]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]], on a scholarship. He was drawn there by coach Bryan Burrell, who he had previously worked with. Moving to Raleigh also allowed him to work closely with his personal trainer, Drew Hanlen.{{cite web |last1=Jeter |first1=Fred |title=John Marshall standout Isaiah Todd transferring |url=https://richmondfreepress.com/news/2018/may/04/john-marshall-standout-isaiah-todd-transferring/ |website=[[Richmond Free Press]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=May 4, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Kolenich |first1=Eric |title=In North Carolina, Isaiah Todd has transformed his team and maybe himself, too |url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/high-school/in-north-carolina-isaiah-todd-has-transformed-his-team-and/article_3c98bf88-30d6-11e9-89f9-d75b5e51caff.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=February 14, 2019}} Todd led the team, which had been coming off two losing seasons, to a 21–12 record while averaging 28 points and 15 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Pope IV |first1=Jonas |title=This UNC basketball target is the No. 1 player in NC. But will he move to Florida? |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/article232535547.html |website=[[The News & Observer]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=July 15, 2019}} He was named ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA North Carolina Player of the Year.{{cite web |title=2018-19 ALL-USA North Carolina Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-north-carolina-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=April 16, 2019}} Todd transferred to another private Christian school in Raleigh, [[Word of God Christian Academy]], for his final high school season, playing under Byron Williams in The Grind Session.{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Chosen 25 forward Isaiah Todd will transfer to Word of God (N.C.) for senior season |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/chosen-25-forward-isaiah-todd-will-transfer-to-word-of-god-n-c-for-senior-season |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=August 1, 2019}} As a senior, he was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], but both games were cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=March 30, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Entering his sophomore season at John Marshall, Todd was ranked as the number one recruit in the 2020 class by [[ESPN]].{{cite web |last1=Shaffer |first1=Jonas |title=Baltimore native rated ESPN's No. 1 hoops prospect in Class of 2020 |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2017/06/23/baltimore-native-rated-espns-no-1-hoops-prospect-in-class-of-2020/ |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |access-date=January 20, 2020 |date=June 23, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Biancardi |first1=Paul |title=Isaiah Todd tops early look at Class of 2020 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/19708817/get-know-class-2020-espn-25-rankings |website=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=January 20, 2020 |date=June 23, 2017}} On October 17, 2019, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], among others. At the time, Todd was a consensus top-15 player in his class.{{cite web |last1=Rapp |first1=Timothy |title=5-Star PF Isaiah Todd Commits to Michigan over Kansas, Kentucky, More |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2840615-5-star-pf-isaiah-todd-commits-to-michigan-over-kansas-kentucky-more |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=January 20, 2019 |date=October 17, 2019}} On April 14, 2020, he decommitted from Michigan and announced that he would forgo his [[college basketball|college]] eligibility to pursue a professional career.{{cite web |last1=Henschke | first1= John | title = Isaiah Todd decommits from Michigan to pursue overseas options| = yes }} ==Professional career== ===NBA G League Ignite (2020–2021)=== On April 17, 2020, Todd signed a one-year contract with the [[NBA G League Ignite]], a developmental team affiliated with the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |title=No. 13-ranked basketball prospect Isaiah Todd signs with G League |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29049520/no-13-ranked-prospect-isaiah-todd-signs-g-league |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=July 16, 2020 |date=April 17, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Five-Star Recruit Isaiah Todd Signs With NBA G League |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/five-star-recruit-isaiah-todd-signs-with-nba-g-league/ |publisher=[[NBA G League]] |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |date=April 17, 2020}} He was drawn to the G League because he wanted to "learn from pros and learn from NBA coaches and trainers."{{cite web |last1=Charania |first1=Shams |title=Isaiah Todd on his decision to join the G League over playing college basketball |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1754160/2020/04/17/isaiah-todd-on-his-decision-to-join-the-g-league-over-playing-college-basketball/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=April 17, 2020 |date=April 17, 2020}} Todd averaged 12.3 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Isaiah Todd |url=https://gleague.nba.com/player/isaiah-todd/ |publisher=[[NBA G League]] |access-date=April 24, 2021}} ===Washington Wizards (2021–2023)=== Todd was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 31st pick by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He was subsequently traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] for the draft rights of the 54th and 60th picks, [[Sandro Mamukelashvili]] and [[Georgios Kalaitzakis]], and two future second-round draft picks.{{cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks Acquire Draft Rights to Two Players in Trade with Indiana Pacers |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/milwaukee-bucks-acquire-draft-rights-two-players-trade-indiana-pacers |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 1, 2021 |date=July 30, 2021}} He was then traded to his hometown team, the [[Washington Wizards]], alongside [[Aaron Holiday]] for the draft rights of [[Isaiah Jackson (basketball)|Isaiah Jackson]], in a five-team trade.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/washington-acquires-six-players-five-team-trade|title=Washington acquires six players in five-team trade|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021}} On January 28, 2022, the Wizards suspended Todd for one game for "conduct detrimental to the team."{{Cite web|title=Wizards suspend Isaiah Todd one game for "conduct detrimental to the team"|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2022/01/28/wizards-suspend-isaiah-todd-one-game-for-conduct-detrimental-to-the-team/|access-date=January 29, 2022|website=NBC Sports}} Todd appeared in 12 games for the Wizards during the 2021–2022 season.{{Cite web |title=Isaiah Todd Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/toddis01.html |access-date=May 1, 2022 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} On June 24, 2023, the Wizards traded Todd, along with [[Jordan Goodwin]] and [[Bradley Beal]], to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for a package that included four first-round pick swaps, six second-round picks, [[Landry Shamet]], and [[Chris Paul]].{{cite web|title=Wizards Agree to Trade Beal to Phoenix, Acquire Paul, Shamet and Draft Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-agree-to-trade-beal-to-phoenix-acquire-paul-shamet-and-draft-picks|website=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2023|access-date=June 24, 2023}} On July 11, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] acquired Todd and the rights to two future first-round pick swaps from the Suns in exchange for three second-round picks.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies acquire rights to two future first-round pick swaps and Isaiah Todd from Suns|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-rights-to-two-future-first-round-pick-swaps-and-isaiah-todd-from-suns|website=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2023|access-date=July 12, 2023}} However, on September 30, they waived him.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Matthew Hurt and Mychal Mulder|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-matthew-hurt-and-mychal-mulder|website=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} ===Return to the Ignite
